plan.summary: This 4-week block starts the 12-week off-camp build for boxing with one efficient full-body session each week. Week 1 establishes training baselines using simple RPE-based work since you are a beginner with minimal home equipment, and Weeks 2-4 build strength, power, and enough conditioning without leaving you too beat up for skill practice. At the end of Week 4, review recovery, boxing workload, and exercise quality before progressing the next block.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general full-body strength and simple explosive qualities while keeping conditioning supportive and recoverable.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main lifts and power work with slightly harder effort while keeping volume tight around boxing training.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Turn the earlier strength gains into faster, sharper output with lower fatigue and higher movement intent.

exercises.name: 1a. Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Bodyweight only. Reset between reps and jump as fast as possible. Land softly and stop if height drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low stable box and step down each rep.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if squat jumps feel awkward.

exercises.name: 1b. Plyo Push-Up to Elevated Surface
exercises.notes: Use a bench, box, or sturdy table so reps stay crisp. Explode up, catch softly, and keep the body straight.

substitutionOptions.name: Fast Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Drive up fast if leaving the surface is not comfortable.

exercises.name: 2. Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Use a load that leaves about 2 reps in reserve. Brace, sit between the hips, and stand up hard.

performanceTarget.prompt: Log your heaviest clean set of 6 each week. Add a small amount only if all reps stay solid.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if one bell is too light.

substitutionOptions.name: Kettlebell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Keep elbows tucked and torso tall.

exercises.name: 3a. Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.notes: Use a load around RPE 7. Pause lightly on the floor, keep shoulders packed, and press with control.

substitutionOptions.name: Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Elevate hands if needed to keep clean reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if you have a stable bench.

exercises.name: 3b. One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Work at RPE 7. Pull the elbow toward the hip and pause briefly at the top without twisting.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if lower-back support is needed.

substitutionOptions.name: Band-Resisted Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if dumbbells are not available.

exercises.name: 4. Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Use a moderate load at RPE 7. Push hips back, keep the back flat, and stop when hamstring tension is strong.

substitutionOptions.name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if kettlebells are available.

substitutionOptions.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a lighter load and stay controlled.

exercises.name: 5a. Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, squeeze glutes, and keep ribs down. Stop before the lower back sags.

substitutionOptions.name: Hard-Style Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use if planks irritate the shoulders.

exercises.name: 5b. Suitcase Carry
exercises.notes: Use a challenging dumbbell or kettlebell. Walk tall and do not lean into the load.

substitutionOptions.name: Suitcase Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Hold for 20-30 seconds each side if space is limited.

exercises.name: 6. Conditioning Circuit
exercises.notes: Move steadily for quality, not exhaustion.

endurancePrescription.rest: 20 seconds between stations, 90 seconds between rounds
